assertions.source: Of {S=0, S=|tr_M|, S=V(𝓑₃,q²)}, only S=0 closes m_p_CODATA to better than 1 ppm; non-zero hypotheses regress by 1000+ ppm. S(p)=0 is calibration-forced.

description: Skein evaluator for the proton's canonical 11-crossing flavored braid. Computes three independent Skein values: (1) V(𝓑₃, t) closed-form Jones polynomial at t = q_0² / q_0 / -q_0⁻¹ conventions; (2) |tr_M(β_p, q_0)| from markov_peel.tr_M_atomic (existing canonical infrastructure); (3) cross-check vs the canonical Layer-1 |tr_M| atlas value 1.0653062286. Closes the S(p) ≈ 0 assumed-zero gap in conj:borromean-baryon-mass-formula.

jones_borromean_at_q0.note: Kauffman 1987 standard t-convention. The Hecke/Jones original substitution is t = q²; the Kauffman bracket uses t = -A⁻², equivalent to t = -q⁻¹ in our convention. The proton's canonical closure is topologically 𝓑₃, so its standalone Jones polynomial equals V(𝓑₃) at any t.

skein_hypothesis_panel.interpretation: Numerically, S(p) ≈ 0 is the ONLY hypothesis consistent with the 1 ppb m_p closure. The candidates |tr_M(β_p)| (~1.07) and V(𝓑₃, q²) (~4.04) would each regress m_p by ~1000 ppm and ~2000 ppm respectively. Therefore the production formula's 'S(p) := 0' is structurally forced by the calibration, not an independent choice. The interpretive question becomes: WHY is the categorical Skein contribution effectively zero in this formula? Plausible answer: λ_p_scale already absorbs the Skein-tower correction, so 'S(p)' as a separate additive term is double-counting. The conjecture should be revised: drop S(p) from the formula entirely, OR re-derive λ_p_scale = (Vol(K_p^eff) - S(p)) / Vol(𝓑₃) with both pieces explicit.
